messages:
carmen_cs: Heads up 1: after today's scoring rollout ~120 accounts lost >15 health points and moved from 'green'->'yellow'. noticed a cluster tied to recent hygiene and playbook note merges.

carmen_cs: sample: ACCT-2147 previous_score=87 new_score=64 changed_at=2025-08-12T09:12Z; reason shows missing recent_touch weight penalty.

ravi_data: thanks. i'm running a delta between scoring versions to isolate which weight change caused the gap. sharing query below.

ravi_data: ```-- compare old vs new weights
SELECT account_id, old_score, new_score, old_recent_touch_weight, new_recent_touch_weight
FROM healthscore_version_deltas
WHERE deploy_id = 'scoring-weights-2025-08-12' AND abs(old_score - new_score) > 10
LIMIT 200;```

playbook-bot: alert: playbook hygiene-merge-v1 merged 312 notes in the 02:00 window; removed_tags=["auto-checkin","template:legacy"].

sophie_rev: are these accounts primarily trial/pilot? we need to prioritize renewals and enablement outreach if so.

carmen_cs: quick breakdown: 120 affected; segments: 80 trial, 25 pilot, 15 enterprise. renewals within 180d = 11, within 90d = 4. exporting owner list now.

ops-bot: export job started: query_id=exp-2612345678-1

ops-bot: export job completed: s3://cs-exports/score_regressions_2612345678.csv (120 rows)

sophie_rev: can we pause automated playbook nudges that rely on healthscore for 4h so we don't accidentally ping customers? i'd rather manual checks for the high-touch renewals.

marc_eng: suggested mitigation: roll back scoring-weights-2025-08-12 to previous config and add a feature-flag gate around the hygiene merge so scoring and playbook act consistently. PR for rollback: github.com/redwood/inference/infra/commit/9f8a2b3

marc_eng: short-term ops call: `POST /ops/playbook/suppress` body `{ "filter": "tags:hygiene", "ttl": "4h", "reason": "scoring-regression-mitigation-2612345678" }`

carmen_cs: ops suppression requested for hygiene-tagged rules. status=202.

ravi_data: root cause note: we lowered recent_touch_weight from 0.25 -> 0.10 in the new weights and also the hygiene merge removed many small 'auto-checkin' notes which the prior score used to bump recency. combined effect caused the drop. proposing revert to recent_touch_weight=0.25 and run a scoring backfill.

marc_eng: i'll queue the weight revert and a controlled backfill in staging. will annotate backfill with audit tag 'score_backfill_2612345678'. estimated runtime 2h for prod window.

sophie_rev: while backfill is running, can we surface the 11 renewal <180d accounts in the SRD high-touch queue? I've added the CSV to our enablement drive and will reassign owners.

ops-bot: high-touch queue updated: tag=ht-score-regression-2612345678, rows_added=11, s3://cs-exports/score_regressions_2612345678.csv#renewal_lt_180

ravi_data: after backfill we'll run an A/B comparison to ensure no unintended score inflation. also adding a monitoring alert: if >5% of accounts change bucket in 24h trigger triage.

marc_eng: rolled back weights in staging and ran integration tests; opened PR for prod rollback and backfill scheduling: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8642

carmen_cs: thanks all. follow-ups: (1) enablement outreach for the 11 renewals, (2) schedule postmortem to discuss hygiene->scoring coupling, (3) create playbook guardrail to respect score-backfill windows. adding to next week's ops retro. :thumbsup:
